arxiv-2202-10077.title: Bilinear magnetoresistance in topological insulators: role of magnetic disorder
arxiv-2202-10077.creator: A. N. Zarezad, A. Dyrdał ∗
arxiv-2202-10077.description: Abstract Bilinear magnetoresistance is a nonlinear transport phenomenon that scales linearly with the electric and magnetic fields, and appears in nonmagnetic systems with strong spin-orbit coupling, such as topological insulators (TIs). Using the semiclassical Boltzmann theory and generalized relaxation time approximation, we consider in detail the bilinear magnetoresistance in an effective model describing surface states of three-dimensional topological insulators.

arxiv-2203-04525.description: Abstract In this letter, we analyze a terrestrial wireless communication network assisted by an aerial intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). We consider a packet scheduling problem at the ground base station (BS) aimed at improving the information freshness by selecting packets based on their AoI.

arxiv-2204-13746.title: CAVES: A Dataset to facilitate Explainable Classification and Summarization of Concerns towards COVID Vaccines*
arxiv-2204-13746.creator: Soham Poddar, Azlaan Mustafa Samad, Rajdeep Mukherjee, Niloy Ganguly, Saptarshi Ghosh
arxiv-2204-13746.description: Abstract . Convincing people to get vaccinated against COVID-19 is a key societal challenge in the present times. As a first step towards this goal, many prior works have relied on social media analysis to understand the specific concerns that people have towards these vaccines, such as potential side-effects, ineffectiveness, political factors, and so on.

arxiv-2302-04165.title: IRTCI: Item Response Theory for Categorical Imputation
arxiv-2302-04165.creator: Adrienne Kline, Yuan Luo
arxiv-2302-04165.description: Abstract Most datasets suffer from partial or complete missing values, which has downstream limitations on the available models on which to test the data and on any statistical inferences that can be made from the data. Several imputation techniques have been designed to replace missing data with stand in values.

arxiv-2311-04583.title: Nonlocal correlations in the asymmetric quantum network
arxiv-2311-04583.creator: Souradeep Sasmal, Shyam Sundar Mahato, A. K. Pan
arxiv-2311-04583.description: Abstract The nonlocality revealed in a multiparty multi-source network Bell experiment is conceptually different than the standard multiparty Bell nonlocality involving a single common source. Here, by introducing variants of asymmetric bilocal as well as trilocal network scenarios, we go beyond the typical bilocal network scenario where both the edge parties have an equal number of measurement settings.

arxiv-2410-15015.title: MambaSOD: Dual Mamba-Driven Cross-Modal Fusion Network for RGB-D Salient Object Detection
arxiv-2410-15015.creator: Yue Zhan, Zhihong Zeng, Haijun Liu, Xiaoheng Tan, Yinli Tian
arxiv-2410-15015.description: Abstract The purpose of RGB-D Salient Object Detection (SOD) is to pinpoint the most visually conspicuous areas within images accurately. While conventional deep models heavily rely on CNN extractors and overlook the long-range contextual dependencies, subsequent transformer-based models have addressed the issue to some extent but introduce high computational complexity.

arxiv-2503-18145.title: Asymptotic states of fast neutrino-flavor conversions in the three-flavor framework
arxiv-2503-18145.creator: Jiabao Liu, Hiroki Nagakura, Masamichi Zaizen, Lucas Johns, Shoichi Yamada
arxiv-2503-18145.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jiabao Liu, Hiroki Nagakura, Masamichi Zaizen, Lucas Johns, Shoichi Yamada. There has been growing evidence that mu- and tau neutrinos are noticeably different due to the emergence of muons in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) and binary neutron star mergers (BNSMs). Recent theoretical studies also suggest that all flavors of neutrinos and antineutrinos inevitably experience some flavor mixing instabilities including fast neutrino flavor conversions (FFC), which corresponds to one of the collective neutrino oscillations powered by neutrino self-interactions.

arxiv-2510-11375.title: Sunspot Observations in 1684 – 1702: John Flamsteed and Philippe de La Hire
arxiv-2510-11375.creator: N.V.Nadezhda Zolotova \orcid 0000-0002-0019-2415, M.V.Mikhail \lnm Vokhmyanin \orcid https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4017-6233
arxiv-2510-11375.description: Abstract In this work, we present an extensive review and detailed analysis of sunspot measurements, drawings, and engravings made by John Flamsteed and, mainly, by Philippe de La Hire during the Maunder minimum. All available information and contemporary knowledge about the sunspot nature are shown. The coordinates, areas, and numbers of sunspots and sunspot groups are reconstructed.

arxiv-2510-14013.title: Maximizing Effectiveness and Equity in Kidney Exchange Programs for Novel Compatibility Paradigms
arxiv-2510-14013.creator: Valentina Peralta Clarke, Faculty of Engineering, Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez, Santiago de Chile, Chile Hans de Ferrante, Eurotransplant, Leiden, The Netherlands Francisco Perez Galarce, Universidad de Las Americas, Faculty of Engineering and Business, Santiago de Chile, Chile Joris van de Klundert*,
arxiv-2510-14013.description: Abstract Kidney Exchange Programs (KEPs) promote access to living donor transplantation for patients suffering from end stage renal disease. The HLA compatibility between transplant recipients and donors plays an important role when solving the matching problems occuring in KEPs. Compatibility defines the feasible solution space and often occurs in a weighted form in the objective function.

arxiv-2512-20063.title: PairFlow: Closed-Form Source-Target Coupling for Few-Step Generation in Discrete Flow Models
arxiv-2512-20063.creator: Mingue Park Jisung Hwang Seungwoo Yoo Kyeongmin Yeo Minhyuk SungKAIST {kicikicik,4011hjs,dreamy1534,aaaaa,mhsung}@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2512-20063.description: Abstract We introduce PairFlow , a lightweight preprocessing step for training Discrete Flow Models (DFMs) to achieve few-step sampling without requiring a pretrained teacher. DFMs have recently emerged as a new class of generative models for discrete data, offering strong performance. However, they suffer from slow sampling due to their iterative nature.

pmc-11415329.title: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) in the management of sepsis
pmc-11415329.creator: Toshiaki Iba, Julie Helms, Jerrold H. Levy
pmc-11415329.description: The mortality rate of sepsis remains high and further increases when complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Consequently, early detection and appropriate management of DIC will be helpful for the management of sepsis. Although overt DIC criteria are often used for diagnosing definitive DIC, it was not designed to detect early-phase DIC.

pmc-12428425.title: Genome-Wide Identification of Solute Carrier Family 12 and Functional Characterization of Its Role in Saline–Alkaline Stress Acclimation in the Ridgetail White Shrimp Exopalaemon carinicauda
pmc-12428425.creator: Shuai Tang, Jiajia Wang, Kuo Yan, Zhixin Yu, Jitao Li
pmc-12428425.description: Solute carrier family 12 (SLC12) encodes electroneutral cation-coupled chloride cotransporters responsible for transmembrane ion transport (Na+, K+, and Cl−), which play a critical role in aquatic osmoregulation. However, the SLC12 gene of Exopalaemon carinicauda (EcSLC12) has not been systematically identified or functionally characterized.

pmc-12477418.title: Neuronal Damage Induced by Gradual Oxidative Stress in iPSC‐Derived Neurons: Implications for Ferroptosis Involvement and ALS Drug Evaluation
pmc-12477418.creator: Hayato Kobayashi, Hitoshi Suzuki‐Masuyama, Hirokazu Tanabe, Hiroshi Kato, Setsu Endoh‐Yamagami
pmc-12477418.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases are not fully understood, but oxidative stress is known to play a central role in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). In this study, we developed a method to induce gradual oxidative stress in induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)‐derived motor neurons and cortical excitatory neurons by omitting antioxidants in the media, aiming to create a platform for studying oxidative stress‐dependent neuronal damage in neurodegenerative diseases.

pmc-12613083.creator: Daiana Alymbaeva, Attila Zsarnovszky, Csaba Szabo, David Sandor Kiss, Tibor Bartha, Gergely Jocsak
pmc-12613083.description: Graphical abstract Introduction Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are synthetic or natural chemicals, often environmental pollutants, that interfere with the endocrine system when humans and animals are exposed to them. EDCs can block natural hormones, as well as function as agonists and antagonists of specific hormones (particularly estrogen and thyroid hormones) (Benvenga et al., 2020, Alsen et al., 2021, Jugan et al.

pmc-12617906.title: Early risk factors for acute chest syndrome in sickle cell anemia: A pediatric study
pmc-12617906.creator: Mohamed Condé, Florie Bouvier, Roselyne Brat, Salim Ferrani, Régis Hankard, Philippe Connes, Georges Dimitrov
pmc-12617906.description: Acute chest syndrome (ACS) is a life-threatening complication of sickle cell anemia (SCA). Most often, ACS occurs during the progression of a painful vaso-occlusive crisis (VOC) in vulnerable patients. The present study aimed to identify early risk factors for ACS progression, focusing on patient assessments in a pediatric Emergency Department.

pmc-12690855.title: Efficacy and safety of esketamine for “treatment resistant depression”: registered report for a systematic review with an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials
pmc-12690855.creator: Florian Naudet, Claude Pellen, Liviu A Fodor, Chiara Gastaldon, Corrado Barbui, Erick H Turner, Estelle Le Pabic, Ioana A Cristea
pmc-12690855.description: BackgroundIn 2019, the FDA and EMA approved intranasal esketamine for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). The current study re-evaluated its efficacy and safety.MethodsThis registered report presents a systematic review and individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis of double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trials (RCTs) assessing intranasal esketamine for TRD.

pmc-13010904.title: Characterization of human immunodeficiency virus drug-resistance mutations among individuals with low-level-viremia in low-income and middle-income countries: A meta-analysis
pmc-13010904.creator: Ibrahim Ahmed El-Imam, Upendo Kayeke Chenya, Jackline Vicent Mbishi, Timothy Antipas Peter, Beatrice Kelvin Mpimo, Nicaise Ndembi, Hafidha Mhando Bakari, Mariam Salim Mbwana, Hassan Fredrick Fussi, Haji Mbwana Ally, Sanad Wael Dababneh, Habib Omari Ramadhani
pmc-13010904.description: BACKGROUNDLow-level viremia (LLV) defined as [human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-RNA 51-999 copies/mL] has been associated with an increased risk of drug resistance and treatment failure. Advances in next-generation sequencing enabled the detection of drug resistance mutations (DRM) among people with LLV.

pmc-13381345.title: Effect of Oliceridine on the Acute Postoperative Pain Management After Elective Cesarean Delivery: A Randomized Non-Inferiority Trial
pmc-13381345.creator: Jing Jiang, Guanghua Yuan, Yuhui Shi, Zhou Zhou, Xinxin Wang, Xiaoqiao Sang, Xiaobao Zhang
pmc-13381345.description: PurposeEffective postoperative analgesia following cesarean delivery is crucial for maternal recovery. Sufentanil, commonly administered via patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA), is associated with dose-dependent adverse effects, particularly gastrointestinal disturbances. Oliceridine, a novel G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, offers the dual advantage of potent analgesia and a reduced risk of opioid-related adverse events.
